extracted.intended_audience: scientists and researchers who want to communicate or engage with public audiences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for scientists to communicate research clearly and effectively to public audiences across channels (online, face-to-face, and with journalists), emphasizing message design, audience relevance, and concise delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, concise communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellent public engagement with science builds on a foundation of clear, concise communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on clarity and brevity when engaging public audiences rather than the extended, precision-focused style used in scientific writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift from scientific to conversational style
rubrics_metrics.description: When communicating with public audiences, shift to the way you would speak when 'off the clock.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain your work as you would to a friend or family member — people who care may still struggle to engage, so adopt a more conversational tone and avoid assuming domain knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with the bottom line
rubrics_metrics.description: Public communication flips the scientific paper approach: the bottom-line is the lead, followed quickly by the 'so what', then supporting details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the key point and relevance to the audience rather than lengthy background and methods; put results or conclusions at the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: State the 'so what' early
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the lead with the 'so what' — explain why the audience should care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After giving the bottom-line, immediately explain the significance or implications before presenting supporting details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make content immediately compelling and relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: In a crowded communication environment, most people won’t read content that is not immediately compelling; capture attention by making the bottom line relevant to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrase key ideas to speak directly to audience interests and weigh what will engage them most.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider tactics like removing jargon to improve engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid technical terms or define them simply; prioritize accessibility over technical precision when appropriate for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance precision with relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh the need for precise language with what is most relevant to your audience and will engage them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide case-by-case whether exact technical wording is necessary or whether a clearer, more relatable phrasing better serves the communication goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define the communication goal first
rubrics_metrics.description: Before designing tactics, consider why you are communicating. What is your communication goal?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the goal to guide selection of audiences, channels, and the words/messages you’ll use to engage them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify appropriate audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: From your communication goal, identify appropriate audience(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be specific about which groups you want to reach; tailor messages to their interests and motivations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft audience-tailored messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase your key ideas to speak directly to an audience’s interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language, examples, and framing that resonate with the identified audience to increase engagement and likelihood of achieving your goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed science where less motivated audiences will find it
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider embedding a discussion of science in places where less motivated audiences might discover them accidentally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use opportunistic placement or contexts (e.g., popular media, community events) to reach people who wouldn’t seek out scientific content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the framework across channels and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework (goal → audience → message) can be applied across communication channels, audiences, and goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the same fundamentals for online, face-to-face, and media/journalist engagement; tailor tactics to the specific channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider channels and modes (online, face-to-face, journalists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections focus on various channels or modes of communication, including online and face-to-face communication, and engaging with journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and adapt tactics appropriate to the medium (e.g., social media brevity, conversational tone in interviews, different preparation for journalists).
